facts.statement: The genus Fujianvenator contains only one species, F. prodigiosus, which is known from a partial articulated skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, F. prodigiosus, known from a partial articulated skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Fujianvenator was discovered in October and November 2022 in the Nanyuan Formation near Yangyuan Village, Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.
facts.quote: The Fujianvenator holotype specimen, IVPP V31985, was discovered during expeditions in October and November 2022 in the Nanyuan Formation near Yangyuan Village in Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.

facts.statement: Xu et al. described Fujianvenator prodigiosus as a new genus and species in 2023.
facts.quote: In 2023, Xu et al. described Fujianvenator prodigiosus as a new genus and species of anchiornithid theropod based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The specific name prodigiosus is derived from the Latin word meaning bizarre.
facts.quote: The specific name, "prodigiosus", is derived from a Latin word meaning "bizarre".

facts.statement: Fujianvenator weighed approximately 641 grams, a size similar to a koklass pheasant.
facts.quote: Fujianvenator weighed approximately 641 g, which is similar in size to the koklass pheasant.

facts.statement: Because its tibiotarsus and metacarpals were unfused, the holotype individual was not skeletally mature when it died.
facts.quote: As the tibiotarsus and metacarpals are unfused, Xu et al. observed that the holotype individual would not have been skeletally mature when it died.

facts.statement: Evidence such as an ossified sternum and fused ankle bones suggests the animal was likely a subadult.
facts.quote: However, the ossified sternum, fused astragalus and calcaneum, and closed sutures of the dorsal vertebrae indicate that the animal was likely a subadult.

facts.statement: In Fujianvenator, the scapula is approximately 40% the length of the humerus.
facts.quote: In Fujianvenator, the ratio is closer to 40%.

facts.statement: Details of its metacarpals suggest Fujianvenator had flexible grasping fingers that could have aided in capturing prey.
facts.quote: Furthermore, details of its metacarpals suggest that Fujianvenator would have had flexible grasping fingers, which could have aided in capturing prey.

facts.statement: Fujianvenator had proportionately long legs, with the tibia being twice as long as the femur.
facts.quote: Fujianvenator had proportionately long legs; the tibia of Fujianvenator is twice as long as the femur.

facts.statement: Its high cursorial score suggests Fujianvenator may have been a particularly adept runner.
facts.quote: The cursorial score of Fujianvenator was much higher than that of troodontids and tyrannosaurids, which are generally accepted to have been adept at running. This may indicate that it was a particularly cursorial animal.

facts.statement: Its limb proportions are similar to wading birds, suggesting it may have had a wading ecology.
facts.quote: Conversely, elongated lower legs are also associated with a wading ecology, as is seen in some extant birds like cranes and storks. The limb proportions of Fujianvenator are similar to wading birds, so this behavior is also possible.

facts.statement: Fujianvenator lived during the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 150.2 to 149.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fujianvenator was discovered in layers of the Nanyuan Formation, which dates to the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic period, about 150.2-149.9 million years old.

facts.statement: Its discovery alongside aquatic and semiaquatic animals suggests Fujianvenator lived in a swamp environment.
facts.quote: The discovery of Fujianvenator with several aquatic and semiaquatic animals suggests that it lived in a swamp environment, which is an unusual ecological niche for an early avialan.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Fujianvenator possibly had a terrestrial or wading lifestyle.
facts.quote: It is suggested to possibly have had a terrestrial or wading lifestyle.
